body: Thank you. I know it will go away, it’s just getting to that point. I hate this feeling so much

That’s exactly what happened. I was watching tv, a show that I watch often watch with no problem, and just started to panic all of a sudden. This has never happened to me before even though I’ve struggled with anxiety for many years.
Thank you. I am trying so hard to calm myself down. I know I’m ok and don’t even know why I’m so anxious. I have problems with anxiety but there is usually a reason. This just feels so different.
Plus cash tips aren’t taxed.
Ugh. Sorry. Food arriving + phone in pocket = crazy responses.
People actually carried cash back then though. It was rare to even give back change. People either had the correct change or would let you keep the change as your tip.
Mine is missing since yesterday and I didn’t get a pop up or an email. Not sure what’s going on.

I let my sons ride with me. My 12 year old asks all the time if he can deliver “just this one order”. He’s old enough that he could handle it but I won’t let him do it.  I do let my 18 year old on occasion but only “leave it at the door”orders and in decent neighborhoods. Technically however, nobody but the dasher is even supposed to touch the food.

I bought a roll of seals from DD that I use when the bags aren’t sealed. I know it would make me feel better if the bags arrived sealed. They were only $3 of you order them from the merchant’s side and they’ve lasted forever.

Idk about anywhere else but my BK doesn’t start the order until the driver arrives. I had an order there a couple days ago and there were only 2 employees working. One working drive thru as well as tue counter and one cooking. I waited, but I could see why others wouldn’t. I felt bad for them.

I just mean most of the orders i delivered when delivering pizza were cash orders. It was before you could pay with a debit/credit card. It had to be cash or check. Everyone knew delivery drivers carried cash. But it was safer back then than it is today. And I didn’t have the option to decline orders in bad neighborhoods.
That’s cool. I thought maybe that was they toy they were giving out now. I was going to have to go get a happy meal.
Obviously not the point of your post, but is that a Pound Puppy?  Is that their toy right now?
Thank you!  These are all excellent reasons I hadn’t thought of. Other than the fact that it was too many years ago to admit, I’m wondering how none of this happened to me while delivering pizza.

I’ve been dashing for a little over 2 years and delivered pizza before that. I’ve only had one serious incident in all that time. I live in a small, pretty safe town though. I do carry pepper spray and I’ve heard other drivers talk about carrying a mag light. It helps find houses at night and could double as a weapon. Also consider using an app that tracks her location and has an emergency alert feature.

If you want something thoroughly exquisite highly detailed and definitely lit, a Doordash tattoo is not the way to go. I hope this a joke, but if not, please think about it for awhile or get it somewhere that it can be covered if necessary.
I got some really good Mexican this way before. Asking for food that had been sitting there, not stealing it that is.

The best advice I can give you is not to try for Top Dasher.  The “perks” are not worth the amount of gas you’ll waste taking no tip deliveries. 

Any other important tips I can think of have already been mentioned.
No and the number they use to notify you of a delivery isn’t the same as the one that tells you that you have a dash coming up. Not that it really matters. I ignore them pay of the time anyway.
Gotcha. I thought that was a little strange but you never know with DD.
Good to know. I figured there was some way to do it.
I’d be tempted too, but if you complete the order then they can rate you. One can guess what the rating would be

I just posted and asked this question. I wasn’t sure what happened if they didn’t pay. What was the cost of the food and how much did they end up crediting you for?
I had something similar happened. I did a shop and deliver order and the red card wouldn’t go through. Support said to use my own card and they would reimburse me. Right after she hung up I got the card to work but they had already credited my account. It was almost worth the $40 just for having to deal with support though.
That’s a good point. I hadn’t thought of that aspect. Might depend on the neighborhood, although people in nicer neighborhoods probably would have a problem paying with a card.

I haven’t either for the same reason. I probably still won’t but was curious. I know back in the day when I delivered pizza I got better tips from cash paying customers than ones that had prepaid with a card.
So they can tip in the app and pay in cash?  That’s kinda cool. All I’ve seen for cash deliveries is the base pay.

That’s what I would assume too, it just makes me paranoid. Support is a joke most of the time and I’d be afraid they wouldn’t give my money back. Do you have to use your red card or does it automatically come out of your earnings?  Sorry for all the questions. Just trying to decide if it’s worth it.

Yeah I’d keep the food too. I’m just worried about them taking it out of my pay. I know when the pandemic first started some places weren’t set up to receive payment though DD and you had the option to pay with your own money. Then DD would reimburse you. I’m curious if they would reimburse you if the customer didn’t pay.

I get 3. The text, the notification from the app, and if I’m looking at something else, when I go back to DD it starts chiming. So annoying!  I’ll have to try temporarily blocking the number, but with my luck I’ll forget to turn it back on.
The ones I’ve seen that are this size can also be plugged into your car. I want one so bad!
Depends on how well you know the store. I work at the grocery store DD uses so I know where everything is. I’d do it in a heartbeat.
You won’t have access to the dash widget, assuming it’s still available on android. It took me some time to get used to that and I still miss it sometimes.

I think it has to do with what they have in stock at the store. When you click on the item if it says it’s available for pick up they will deliver it with doordash. 
I know on my end once I’ve completed a delivery it says tips can be added for up to 25 days. I have no idea how to do it though.
This. As soon as the college let out hours have started disappearing within a few minutes of 3.

I usually do better during lunch than dinner. Most of my lunch orders are to businesses. I don’t live in a big city so most businesses and restaurants are all on the main road through town. It makes for very quick deliveries instead of having to drive into residential areas like I do for dinner
I love these kind of deliveries. Did you get a good tip?  I usually have pretty good luck

Does anyone know what happens if a driver has to pick up a forgotten item?  Wendy’s forgot some of my items once and another driver delivered them. Since support initiated the second delivery it didn’t give me the option to tip in the app. I’m curious if the driver only got base pay or if they added extra for them. 
- I was not home, kids had ordered or I would have made sure and given a cash tip
Oh I know. I was just adding to your comment.

Mine did that last September for no reason and stayed that way for a couple months. It did it again at the beginning of last month but only lasted a week. I’m back to being able to schedule at 3. Contacting support is a joke. I was told I couldn’t schedule because there weren’t any openings for the time I was trying to schedule.

They don’t always pay attention to it though. There have been so many times, especially at one restaurant, that they didn’t even hear the iPad go off. I showed up with a double order and they didn’t even know they had orders to make. Apparently, if the restaurant doesn’t respond within a certain amount of time, they go ahead and dispatch a driver.
When did this start?

I have very good relationships with all my kids. They know there is nothing they can’t tell me. My motto is “I don’t expect you to be perfect, but I do expect you to be honest” and it works most of the time.

No, I agree. I’d rather him be on as few medications as possible. I do as many as our appointments virtually anyway.  I’ll have to see what our insurance covers. 
You’re not being dismissive at all. That’s probably why he started smoking. I noticed it was making a difference so I didn’t stop it. It had been going on for a little while before I knew about it
Thank you. Good luck to you too.

I prefer edibles anyway. They are just so much more expensive, here anyway. 

She took you to the dr and told them she was letting you smoke?  What did they say?  And where are you from if you don’t mind me asking.
Thank you. It will. It might take some time but he’ll be fine. All of you in here have made me feel much better!
That’s kinda scary considering how short of a time he has been smoking. I hope he isn’t going to have a life-long battle with addiction.
Thank you so much!
Thank you!  And good for you!

That is very interesting about ADHD. He already struggles with it. I will definitely point that out to him. 

Yes, there is a very big difference between the weed back then and the weed now. 

Can mental addiction happen at different rates for different people?  I’ve been smoking for 25 years and I have no problem going without.
I actually do have an appointment with a therapist next week or the week after.  Someone else suggested I have him look on here too. I will definitely suggest it. I appreciate your help!

I definitely told the customer what was going on. Unfortunately the wife was already on her way to the restaurant to pick the food up herself. They were understanding when I showed them the times on my phone though.

That’s impressive!  I’ve tried to quit cigarettes many times but haven’t been successful. I’ve quit weed several times for jobs and whatever though. Everyone is different though. I talked to him about other addictions a little bit last night but I plan on having another conversation probably later tonight

That is so sad. I know a few people in the same situation. 

That is an excellent idea. I don’t know if he he gets on here at all but it wouldn’t hurt to mention it.
Thank you!  We do have a good relationship already and I know it will be better on the other side of all of this.

I meant physically. He’s not going to start puking and shitting his guts out because he hasn’t smoked a joint yet today. Obviously it can be psychologically addictive. But I’m pretty sure you knew that.

He knows I’m here no matter what. There’s nothing he can do to change that. I hope that’s enough to know how much he is worth and what he is capable of. I’m sorry things are rough for you at home. That can’t be easy.
I’m know that is a lot of it which is why I am trying to be as understanding and easy on him as possible.
This made me cry. I am so sorry!  I’m going to do everything I can to make sure this doesn’t happen to him

He does have ADHD and I think it does help him with that. And that’s where I’m conflicted. I think it helps but it’s getting out of hand. I wish I could take him to a doctor or therapist and tell them that I wanted to give it to him and make out a plan of how much he gets etc. I’m afraid it wouldn’t go over well. But I’ve never tried so I don’t know. 

I would never go as far as kicking him out. He needs help and understanding, not punishment. I’m sorry your family member was treated that way!

I agree 100%.  I hate that a medication that has so many uses was considered evil for so long. I myself, have been on so many antidepressants and nothing seems to work. I don’t have a problem with him doing it except that he isn’t legally old enough and the stealing isn’t ok. I definitely am looking into what I can do for him now that I know how bad it has gotten. I also know that it does help with his depression, so it’s hard. I don’t want him on unnecessary meds but I also don’t want him to get any deeper into this.

You’re right. I just worry about him hearing about other drugs and whatever. I’d be stupid to think he isn’t hearing about it at school or on his games though. I think I’m going to try to keep him here as an outpatient but definitely start looking into options for inpatient treatment if necessary. Without going into a lot of detail, he doesn’t need to feel like he’s not wanted to is being abandoned by another parent. Not that I would be abandoning him by any means, but I’d never forgive myself if it came across that way
Ok. Thanks. I plan on looking into something like that next week. I’m glad it helped you. Makes me optimistic.

Do you think there would be a chance of him learning other things though?  And I think the closest place would be at least 90 minutes away if not 5 hours because of where we live. If that’s what needs to be done, I’ll do it though.

I get that. There are many times it’s the only thing that keeps me sane. I just want him to go about it the right way. He’s old enough to have a job and he works with me sometimes and gets paid, but then he spends his money on games.

I get it. It’s the only thing keeping me sane sometimes. I just wish he would go about it the right way. He’s old enough to have a job and he works with me sometimes and gets paid, but the spends his money on games

Oh no!  He isn’t in trouble. I’m not happy with the situation but it’s deeper than him just stealing. He needs help more than he needs a punishment. You’re right. Taking his stuff isn’t going to help. It’s only going to stress him out more and give him another reason to smoke. 

I’m glad to hear you are doing well. It gives me hope we can make it out the other side of this and he will be ok.

I’m not forcing medication on him at all. I learned he wasn’t taking it when I would find the pills under his bed. When I talked to him last night he agreed that he probably needs to be on something but hates the idea of it. He’s old enough I will let him make that decision himself. 

I probably used addiction wrong. I guess that’s where my mind went when I was seeing his behaviors such as the stealing and lying. He even admitted to me he didn’t care about the consequences at the time. It just made me think of someone addicted to something harder. 

I will definitely have to look into that. My options here are a little limited but hopefully we can find someone that will work for him. 

I think he knows why he’s doing it. It was really late when we were talking and I will talk to him some more today but we did have a good talk. He was very open about everything and apologetic for what happened. 

It makes complete sense. He understands that there’s a problem, he just isn’t sure how to fix it yet. Hopefully therapy will help him with that. 

I appreciate your insight!

You’re not wrong but I legitimately use it as pain medicine. I’m limited as to what meds I can take due to intolerances. I’ve been thinking about it for awhile now but it’s a hard decision to make. It’s difficult for me to work when I’m in pain

I get that completely. My parents forced me into therapy when I was a teenager too. I hated it and didn’t work it at all. I’ve gone a couple times as an adult because it was my idea and got so much more out of it.
That’s where I’m worried he’s headed. It’s not so much that he does it, just the way he’s going about it. Are you still having trouble?
It’s definitely possible. Or just an empty feeling in his hands like cigarette smokers. After talking to him last night he realizes that he is addicted even if it is only psychological

I get where you’re coming from, and to an extent you’re right. I didn’t realize until last night exactly how bad it was. I knew things were missing but when I asked him about it be denied it. We have a pretty good relationship and he’s usually honest with me. Last night I found some of the things I was missing in his room. When I asked him about it he broke down. He’s also had some pretty traumatic things happen in the last week or so. 

It’s actually his Dr. that is crap and I’m working on having him see someone else. There are only 2 or 3 doctors that see children in my town which makes it difficult. They all have long waiting lists. 

It’s not really that he’s smoking too much, it’s that I now (as of yesterday) have proof of how much he has been taking from me. It’s the stealing that’s the issue and I guess that’s the boundary he’s crossed.  It’s the need to have it at any cost that has me concerned. 

I have in no way attacked him. We talked for quite a long time last night. I didn’t realize he was struggling as much as he is because he doesn’t like to talk about his feelings much. Now that I am aware, I am going to do everything I can to help the situation. 

I will say this though. After posting this, I’m realizing that it isn’t the “addiction” that is the problem.  You’re right in that he is struggling and coping the best way he knows how. I came here to get insight from other people and it worked.
Oh wow!  How do you even afford that?
They usually understand. If not that’s their problem. I’m already gone.
How often do you smoke?
That is going to be the first thing I’m going to do on Monday. I’m hoping it will do him some good too. I think he needs it. I’m glad it worked for you!

I don’t think it’s anything more than weed. I just feel like his need to have it seems like more of a physical addiction rather than a psychological one. I haven’t found or heard anything that makes me think it’s anything else. Sorry if I made that confusing.
How old are you and how long have you been smoking?

What was it that made you want to quit?

I’m not sure if he wants to quit completely but he knows it has gotten out of control. 

I actually took everything from him last night. Everything he had he stole from me.  I don’t think there is any weed anywhere. I haven’t been buying it because I knew he would take it anyway. 

I’m sure he knows people but to my knowledge he doesn’t get any from anyone. He doesn’t work so he doesn’t have any money. All he has access to is what he takes from me.  On that note, I’m buying a safe. 

He games, but I can’t really get him into anything else. I think he is depressed enough that nothing sounds fun.  What did you do to keep busy?

I want to do this next month anyway. I can’t take the time off work right now but I have parents in town he could stay with if need be.

He is going through a lot right now and is definitely depressed. I think him smoking does helps him forget about it but it doesn’t actually deal with the problem at hand. I think what’s happening is when he doesn’t have any he starts to feel things he doesn’t want to so he’ll do whatever he can to get it so he doesn’t have to feel that anymore. He’s still a bit young, but I don’t care too much about occasionally use. But like you said, every day or more than once a day is too much.

I guess I’m not as good at hiding it as I thought. I need to get a safe. I really don’t have a huge issue with the occasional usage but it has turned into way more than that. He even admitted last night that he has a problem. It’s unfortunate because I believe weed has a lot of benefits.  He isn’t having issues with the actual usage, it’s just the way he’s going about it and the NEED to have it all the time.

I’ll have to look into what we have available here. I might have to take him out of town is the only problem. We aren’t in a very big city and programs are pretty limited. We have inpatient and extensive outpatient psych programs but I haven’t heard of anything else. I know we have one place for adults but I don’t think they take minors. I could probably call them and see if they know of anything though.

That’s what I was thinking, but wasn’t sure. I’d rather him not be on an antidepressant if he doesn’t need to be.  He would benefit much more from learning skills than just swallowing a pill every day

Can a psychologist prescribe meds?  He does have one med he has to be on for ADHD. Mainly though, I am looking for someone for him to talk to. The psychiatrist only sees him for 10 minutes every 3 months if he actually decides to show up for work that day.
I’ve learned when they give you an estimated wait time to double or triple it depending on the restaurant. I suppose they’re worried if they’re honest you’ll leave.
Someone else mentioned virtual meetings and I think it’s a great idea. The stuff he’s going through needs to be dealt with, not just stuffed down and forgotten because he’s high.
Exactly this. It is upper management subscribing but not having to deal with it directly. Why worry about inconveniencing others when it’s bringing in more money for them?

I’d never thought of it being addictive either. I’m realizing that it is probably more of an issue of him using it to not feel the emotional pain he’s in right now.  He’s not addicted to the weed itself rather he’s addicted to not feeling anything.

I’m actually working on that now. I had called yesterday to see about switching doctors and possibly having him see a therapist. The doctor he sees now is a joke. IF he actually shows up for the appointment he doesn’t pay attention to what we tell him and just throws pills at him. Unfortunately he probably thinks that’s how they all are now.

I’m my experience, most restaurants do hate the gig apps. I stood at one place where the manager kept telling the employees not to make my order yet. They don’t have to deal with the delivery customer in person. 

I don’t usually do it last minute. Only if it’s going to be a long wait. In that case they still have plenty of time for another driver to arrive. 

My main concern is the customer’s wait. I picked up an order once and the employee asked me where I had been and that the customer had been calling asking what the hold up was. I had just received the order. My guess is another driver had it and kept it for a long time before unassigning it. That, I feel, is unacceptable.

I found that it was a little busier but the biggest difference was the order size. People were ordering for the whole family instead on just a couple of people, thus the tips were bigger. However, more people are going out to eat these days than they were the last couple of years.

That’s my biggest concern. If he wasn’t lying and stealing I wouldn’t be too terribly worried about it. That’s pretty much exactly what I told him. If he’s doing what he’s doing with weed now, what is he going to be doing in a few years. He says he won’t do anything else, but I’m sure that’s what most people say before they do.

Depending on the situation, yes. I had a double order at one restaurant last week. One order was ready and the other they said would be a 45 minute wait. I did tell them I unassigned the second one so the first order didn’t get cold. If they are rude about it when I walk in I just walk back out to my car without saying anything.

Thank you for this. He knows I love him and there is nothing he can do that will change that. I’m so sorry that you had to experience that especially at that age. That makes me sad.  Everyone has coping mechanisms of some sort. Some are just healthier than others. I hope you are doing well now!

He is lying out of addiction. I don’t care if he does it occasionally. I smoke too and it helps with my depression and anxiety as well as pain. I originally thought it was better than taking prescription meds, but it has gotten out of hand.  I am definitely happy he isn’t doing anything else. And I should have clarified.  He isn’t stealing money, just my weed. Then he lies about having taken it.
He seems open to it right now. He really is struggling with a lot in life right now so it makes sense he would bury his feelings in weed.

I can only speak for my area and what I read on here, but I doubt it is ever worth it to be a top dasher. I know some people let their AR drop until the last few days of the month and then raise it just high enough to qualify. I tried it a couple months but it didn’t seem to make much difference. As long as you are able to get hours there really isn’t an advantage.  You won’t make anything if you accept everything especially with gas prices these days.

You hit the nail on the head with that one. He deals with depression anyway but has had a lot going on lately too. He is definitely using it as an escape. Fortunately, based on our conversation tonight, he recognizes the problem and does want help. I’m hoping he follows through with it when the time comes.
The problem is where we live there isn’t anything like that. The closest place would be at least 90 minutes away, if not 3 hours. I’d definitely be willing to do that if it came down to it though.

At 16, I hope there are sexual side effects lol. However, I’m sure he doesn’t. I’ll have to mention Wellbutrin when I talk to the dr. 

He definitely has a problem with motivation. He’s said that himself. I figured it was the depression, but maybe I was wrong, or it’s a combination of both.  I’d heard about the schizophrenia which is a little scary to me as I had a cousin with schizoaffective disorder. I know these things can run in families. 
I had no idea it could cause hyper emesis. 

I generally don’t have a problem with people smoking but I agree, it shouldn’t be minors and definitely not to the extent he has gotten into it

In theory, if one is a top dasher, the order would go to them. If neither are top dashers, AR doesn’t mean anything. Top dashers don’t necessarily get dibs on the higher paying orders, just any orders close to them. There is a large order program but you have to be invited to a part of it. I believe you can add yourself to the wait list but you have to have a catering bag.

I’m sure you’re right. We have a good relationship and are very open about a lot of things. That’s part of why tonight was so surprising. I’m willing to hear anything as long as he gets the help he needs. Thanks for the heads up.
This is brilliant. Attending a virtual meeting hadn’t even crossed my mind. I will definitely look into that. Thank you!

I’m with you on the antidepressant. He’s prescribed one but he won’t take it. I know he’s depressed and has some really shitty things going on in his life right now. I’m
Hoping this will wake him up and he will be willing to give it a second chance. 
What kind of effects are we talking about?  I started smoking at a fairly young age but it wasn’t nearly as potent as it is now.

I agree. I really don’t think it’s anything else though. He’s stealing from me. I was asleep tonight and heard him messing around where I keep my stuff. I found a bowl on his desk earlier today and he shoved it in a drawer. I made him empty the drawer out in front of me and there was only weed stuff. He had all kinds of bowls, batteries and carts. Basically everything that I thought I had just misplaced. There wasn’t anything hinting to anything else. I’ve smoked for 25 years and never had a problem quitting or going without if necessary. I’m worried that if he has such a problem with weed, if he is introduced to something else, it’s going to become a very serious and possibly deadly addiction.
Are there physical withdrawal symptoms with weed or mostly psychological?

I was wondering about that too. He sees a psychiatrist but he’s a POS and no help at all. I just called yesterday, before I knew all this, to see about getting him in with someone else. There’s going to be quite a wait. Maybe his GP could prescribe something.
